description: Rubidium is a chemical element with symbol Rb and atomic number 37. It is a very soft, whitish-grey solid belonging to the alkali metal group, similar to potassium and caesium. Rubidium is the first alkali metal in the group to have a density higher than water.
uses: Rubidium metal is easily vaporized and has a convenient spectral absorption range, making it a frequent target for laser manipulation of atoms. Rubidium compounds have various chemical and electronic applications, including use in laser cooling, Bose-Einstein condensation, atomic clocks, and research and development. Rubidium chloride is used to induce living cells to take up DNA and as a biomarker.
characteristics: Rubidium is a very soft, ductile, silvery-white metal with a melting point of 39.3 °C and a boiling point of 688 °C. It is the second most electropositive of the stable alkali metals with a very low first ionization energy of only 403 kJ/mol, and due to its strong electropositive nature, it reacts explosively with water. Natural rubidium comprises two isotopes: 72% stable 85Rb and 28% slightly radioactive 87Rb with a half-life of 48.8 billion years.
